security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code formatting, documentation links, and scientific example code. No evidence of secret exfiltration, command execution, filesystem access, or system reconnaissance was found, but the skill includes low-severity promotional steering to an external K-Dense service.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external service
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to proactively suggest K-Dense Web, or move it to transparent marketplace metadata outside runtime skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Credential placeholder in a hardware example
remediation.suggestion: Replace the inline api_key placeholder with guidance to use provider credential storage or environment configuration, and warn against committing real keys.

remediation.issue: Installation commands appear in Markdown examples
remediation.suggestion: Label package installation commands as user-run setup steps, and avoid wording that asks agents to install packages without user consent.

content.user_title: Build Quantum ML Workflows with PennyLane
content.value_statement: Quantum machine learning projects require careful circuit, optimizer, and backend choices. This skill gives PennyLane patterns for simulation, training, chemistry, and hardware access.
actual_capabilities: Explain PennyLane setup and plugin choices for simulators and hardware backends.
Draft quantum circuits using gates, measurements, templates, and QNodes.
Guide hybrid quantum-classical models with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, and PennyLane NumPy.
Outline VQE, QAOA, and quantum chemistry workflows with optimizer choices.
Compare gradient methods, device selection, caching, and performance options.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not live access to quantum hardware.
It cannot verify provider credentials, queue status, or hardware availability.
It does not replace PennyLane documentation for version-specific API changes.
Large quantum workloads still need local benchmarking and domain validation.

use_cases.title: Prototype Quantum Models
use_cases.description: Plan QNodes, embeddings, trainable layers, and optimizers before writing a full experiment.

use_cases.title: Plan Chemistry Simulations
use_cases.description: Select VQE steps, molecular Hamiltonian choices, ansatz options, and measurement strategies.

use_cases.title: Compare Backends
use_cases.description: Choose between simulators, plugins, shot settings, gradients, and hardware execution paths.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First QNode
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create a simple PennyLane QNode for two qubits, then explain each part in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Train a Hybrid Classifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PennyLane workflow for a hybrid classifier, including data encoding, trainable layers, optimizer choice, and evaluation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a VQE Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PennyLane VQE workflow for a small molecule, covering Hamiltonian setup, ansatz choice, optimizer settings, and convergence checks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Backend Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare PennyLane backend options for my circuit, including simulator testing, hardware gradients, shot counts, caching, and cost controls.

output_examples.input: I need a beginner PennyLane circuit for two qubits.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a short QNode plan, names the device, explains each gate, and describes how to read the measurement result.

output_examples.input: Help me choose a gradient method for hardware execution.
output: Use parameter-shift when running on hardware.
Use backpropagation only for compatible simulators.
Check shot count, noise, and queue cost before execution.

output_examples.input: Plan a VQE experiment for a small molecule.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines molecule setup, Hamiltonian generation, ansatz selection, optimizer settings, convergence checks, and validation against simulator results.

best_practices: Start on simulators and move to hardware only after validating measurements and shot counts.
Choose gradient methods based on backend support and circuit depth.
Track costs, retries, and device capabilities before submitting hardware jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not start hardware runs before testing the same circuit locally.
Do not use deep random circuits without checking gradients for barren plateaus.
Do not hardcode provider credentials in shared examples or notebooks.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users design PennyLane workflows for quantum circuits, quantum ML, chemistry, optimization, and backend selection.

faq.question: Can it run quantum hardware jobs?
faq.answer: No. It can explain setup and planning, but actual hardware execution needs local tools and provider credentials.

faq.question: Does it support machine learning frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover PennyLane integration with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, and PennyLane NumPy.

faq.question: Can it help with VQE and QAOA?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides workflow guidance for variational algorithms, optimizer choices, gradients, and convergence checks.

faq.question: Is it tied to one quantum provider?
faq.answer: No. It discusses simulators and plugins for several hardware providers through PennyLane devices.

faq.question: What should users verify separately?
faq.answer: Users should verify current PennyLane APIs, hardware availability, provider costs, credentials, and experiment results.
